key_idea: Toppings are vertices and slices are edges: after removing duplicates, an edge to a neighbour that has any other slice must sit at one of the two ends of a topping's arc, so the 'core' (vertices with a loop or >=2 distinct neighbours) must have max degree 2, and a core cycle must be the only component.
sketch: Deduplicate slices (identical slices can sit next to each other) and separate loops. Call a topping core if it has a loop or at least two distinct neighbours; pure leaves can be placed inside their neighbour's arc. If some core vertex has more than 2 core neighbours it is impossible. Otherwise each component's core is a path or a cycle (caterpillar-like structure): paths can be laid out linearly and concatenated around the circle, while a cycle needs the whole circle, so it is possible only if that component is the only one (count components over used toppings with DSU, cycle iff core edges >= core vertices). O(n log n). Pitfalls: loops make a leaf count as core, multi-edges must not create fake 2-cycles, unused toppings are not components. Stress-tested against a permutation brute force on 1500 random small cases.
